call_points.text: AdColony assets to activate over 100,000 mobile apps and reach 500 million connected devices in Developed Markets this year.
Larger acquisition is in third-party due diligence; management aims to close by early 2027 and says it must be EPS- and cash-flow-accretive.
Management expects better margin expansion within this financial year, especially in Developed Markets, helped by AdColony.
Direct advertiser revenue was about 79% of the quarter versus 74% for FY2026; management gave no guidance on the mix.
Vertical ranking in India and Emerging Markets is E, F, H then G; RMG (category G) is still in a recovery phase.
On Bobble, where ₹136 Cr is invested, no impairment was taken; it will be tested once the NCLT appeal is decided.
Management said it sees no impact on connected-device additions from higher memory prices lifting device costs.
Average CPCU rate is now above ₹60; currency-adjusted pass-through to advertisers has trimmed margins in the short term.
Management maintained medium-term 20% organic CAGR target, progressing toward a decadal 10x growth vision.
Gross margin compression from data/inventory investments will take about a year before delivering higher margins.
Geopolitical events caused temporary softness in select markets/verticals in Q4, but CPCU model maintained positive sequential growth.

penalties.authority: Collector of Stamps (HQ) Govt. of NCT Delhi
penalties.details: The Collector of Stamps (HQ) Govt. of NCT Delhi raised a query on the stamp duty paid by us on allotment of 48,450 equity shares to Affle (India) Limited Employees Welfare Trust. Although stamp duty at the rate of 0.005% was duly paid through the NSDL portal, the Collector of Stamps contended that, since the Company's registered office is in Delhi, stamp duty was payable at the rate of 0.1% of the market value of the shares as per applicable rates in Delhi. Accordingly, additional stamp duty of Rs. 50,872.50 was paid and a penalty of Rs. 12,000 was imposed on the Company. In the absence of clarity regarding the applicable rate on the allotment of shares, the Company paid the additional stamp duty and penalty amount. The matter has been closed

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹724.38 Cr, net profit ₹119.51 Cr.
Affle 3i reported Q4 FY2026 consolidated revenue of ₹724.4 Cr and PAT of ₹119.5 Cr.
Affle 3i Limited submitted the audio recording of its Q4 FY2026 earnings conference call held on May 11, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. (IST) via its Investor Relations website, signed by Parmita Choudhury.
Affle 3i issued a postal ballot notice for a ₹1,100.38 Cr preferential warrant issue to Affle Holdings Pte. Ltd.
ICRA's monitoring agency report for the March 2026 quarter showed ₹238.32 Cr of Affle's ₹737.43 Cr preferential issue proceeds utilised, with ₹499.11 Cr unutilised and no material deviation.
Affle 3i held its Q4FY26 earnings call, reiterating 20% organic CAGR guidance and highlighting an ₹1,100 Cr promoter warrant issue for M&A.

On 17 August 2026 Affle filed the transcript of its 10 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, where it reported revenue of ₹747 Cr (up 20.4% YoY) and PAT of ₹128 Cr (up 21.7%), and said its larger acquisition was in third-party due diligence with a target to close by early 2027.
Affle 3i received USD 34.99 million from Affle Holdings for the exercise of convertible warrants.
On 16 October 2026 Affle 3i said the Supreme Court had stayed the CIRP proceedings against Bobble pending before the NCLT, with the carrying value of its investment still subject to the appeal.
Affle 3i allotted 17,04,324 equity shares to Affle Holdings upon conversion of warrants at ₹1,115.25 per warrant.
Affle 3i allotted 12,77,155 equity shares on October 21, 2026, pursuant to warrant conversion by the promoter.
